newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Gov has not told Bank/Portugal to sell gold - source.
newsitem.headline: Gov has not told Bank/Portugal to sell gold - source.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal has received no indication from the government that it should sell part of its gold reserves, an official central bank source said.
"There has been no concrete suggestion from the government in this sense," the source told Reuters.
He was speaking after Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said Portugal may sell part of its substantial gold reserves.
"Portugal, which holds a large proportion of its reserves in gold, had for some years and still has the possibility to sell part of its gold reserves," Mateus told TSF radio.
"The previous statement of the governor (to Expresso weekly) is still valid," the central bank source said.

Bank of Portugal governor Antonio De Sousa told Expresso in an interview published on October 6 that Portugal was not planning to sell some of its gold reserves to help it meet convergence criteria for entry to the European single currency.
"The Bank of Portugal is not thinking of selling gold at this time," De Sousa said. "There has been no suggestion from the government to this effect."
